title: Ultrasensitive MoS 2 /In 2 O 3  heterojunction transistor biosensors for glucose detection
content: Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) possesses high biocompatibility and surface activity, enabling efficient biomolecular recognition and detection. Field-effect transistor (FET)-based biosensors have the advantages of high sensitivity and fast response. In this study, we fabricated monolayer MoS2 films by chemical vapor deposition, indium oxide (In2O3) films by magnetron sputtering, and MoS2/In2O3 vertical heterojunction films by a transfer process. FETs based on MoS2, In2O3 and the MoS2/In2O3 vertical heterojunction were then fabricated, and their electrical properties and biosensing performance were analyzed and compared with each other. The fabricated FET devices exhibit good electrical performance. The glucose detection sensitivity of the MoS2/In2O3 FET biosensor is 363.31 mA mM−1 and the limit of detection is 41 nM, which is significantly improved compared with that of the MoS2 FET biosensors with a sensitivity of 120.04 mA mM−1 and the In2O3 FET biosensors with a sensitivity of 70.53 mA mM−1. This improvement is attributed to the heterostructure formed at the MoS2–In2O3 interface, which modulates electron transfer and enables electrons to spontaneously migrate from the low-work-function In2O3 semiconductor to the high-work-function MoS2 semiconductor. The MoS2/In2O3 FET sensors exhibit good stability, selectivity, and reproducibility and can be fabricated on flexible substrates. The device has been tested every 5 days over a period of 25 days, and the device has maintained good stability. The relative standard deviation calculated for this reproducibility test was found to be 4.63%. This study demonstrates that the MoS2/In2O3 heterojunction FET has broad application prospects in glucose sensing.
